pages.text: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs Commerce APIs MCP Reseller APIs Templates Custom Code Upcoming Changes Getting Started Overview Authentication and permissions OAuth Making requests Retrieve basic site information Using Commerce APIs Webhooks Contacts Analytics Discounts Products Websites Inventory Orders Transactions Profiles WebhookSubscriptions Schemas Menu Copy page Getting Started Overview of Commerce APIs With Squarespace Commerce APIs, you can build applications to manage the commerce features of a Squarespace merchant site. Analytics API: Retrieve aggregated commerce data (order counts, totals, donations) for contacts in bulk. Contacts API: Manage the people associated with a site â customers, subscribers, donors â including their address books and marketing preferences. Discounts API: Manage discounts for a site, including their eligibility criteria, discount amount, and activation trigger. Inventory API: Read and adjust stock information for product variants. Orders API: Access order history for one-time purchases and subscription orders or import orders from third-party sales channels. Products API: Manage physical, service, gift card, and download products, including their images and variants (if supported). Profiles API: Read customers, mailing list subscribers, and donors. Now in maintenance mode â new integrations should use the Contacts API . Transactions API: Access financial transactions for orders and donations. Webhook Subscriptions API: Subscribe to notifications from a site, like when an order was created, by configuring a webhook endpoint. Structure and design All Commerce APIs are built on HTTPS and designed with REST principles in mind. Every endpoint uses HTTPS features such as authentication, standard verbs, and standard response status codes. In addition, APIs that support resource updates via POST allow partial updates. Authentication for Commerce APIs also provides permissions to keep Squarespace merchant site data private and secure. Next steps Become familiar with commerce terms and how they're related to the APIs Learn how to send authenticated requests Read the FAQ for answers to common questions Read our brand guidelines Authentication and permissions On this page Structure and design Next steps

pages.title: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs
pages.text: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs Commerce APIs MCP Reseller APIs Templates Custom Code Upcoming Changes Getting Started Overview Authentication and permissions OAuth Making requests Retrieve basic site information Using Commerce APIs Webhooks Contacts Analytics Discounts Products Websites Inventory Orders Transactions Profiles WebhookSubscriptions Schemas Menu Copy page Getting Started Authentication and permissions To keep Squarespace merchant site data private and secure, every request to Commerce APIs must be authenticated and have minimum permissions. However, authenticated requests automatically have access to public site data, such as site name, identifier, language, currency, time zone, and location. Read the permission levels for each Commerce API below. Then, depending on your development needs, authenticate requests by using an API key or OAuth access token. Remember: Requests only have access to data for the website that owns the API key or OAuth access token. API permission levels Forms API Read Only : View form submission data; for Zapier integration only Inventory API Read Only : View inventory stock levels Read and Write : Manage inventory stock levels Orders API Read Only : View order, fulfillment, and customer information (name, email, address, and more) Read and Write : View customer information (name, email, address, and more); manage order and fulfillment information Products API Read Only : View product information, including information for any images and variants; view Store Page information Read and Write : Manage product information, including information for any images and variants; view Store Page information Contacts API Read Only : View contact records, address books, and marketing preferences Read and Write : Manage contact records, address books, and marketing preferences Discounts API Read Only : View discount records Read and Write : Manage discount records Webhook Subscriptions API (OAuth only) Read and Write : Create, update, delete, and test webhook subscriptions Profiles API (maintenance mode â new integrations should use the Contacts API ) Read Only : View the name, address, email, marketing preferences, and other profile information of customers, subscribers, and other website users Transactions API Read Only : View transactional order, donation data, and customer information (email) Authenticating requests Depending on your development needs, you can use a generated API key or start the OAuth process with Squarespace to become a registered OAuth client. A Squarespace merchant site can use both API keys and OAuth for data access, but Squarespace Extensions are required to use OAuth. Custom applications With Squarespace's Commerce Advanced plan, you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site. Follow the steps below to generate an API key for a custom application. Log in to a Squarespace site. In the left nav, click Settings ; scroll down and click Advanced . Click Developer API Keys . Click the GENERATE KEY button. In the dialog, add a key name under "KEY NAME", and select one or more Commerce APIs under "PERMISSIONS" and permission level. Record the generated key in a safe and secure place. For security reasons, this is the only time the API key is visible. API keys will never expire as long as the merchant site remains active. Commercial development Squarespace Extensions allow customers on any plan to optimize and expand their site in a few clicks. If you'd like to develop a new Extension, start the OAuth client process here . Once you've obtained OAuth credentials, you can use our OAuth 2.0 Guide to learn how to authorize your application to integrate with Squarespace and use Squarespace APIs. Registering an OAuth client, and having it reviewed and approved, only allows OAuth connections with Squarespace. It doesn't list your application in Squarespace Extensions , which is a separate process. Next steps Make requests to Commerce APIs Read the FAQ for answers to common questions Read our brand guidelines Overview OAuth On this page API permission levels Authenticating requests Custom applications Commercial development Next steps

pages.text: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs Commerce APIs MCP Reseller APIs Templates Custom Code Upcoming Changes Build on Squarespace Everything you need to build and publish external apps â reliable APIs, clear documentation, and a marketplace to reach Squarespace's global customer base. Read the docs Start building What can you build on Squarespace? Integration, customization, or extension. Our docs can get you started, and the rest is up to you. 01 App creation Use our APIs to connect your business to Squarespace and reach more customers. 02 Advanced commerce management Manage your storefront's orders, inventory, transactions, and more. 03 Website & domain reselling Add Squarespace websites and domains to your business offering. 04 Custom themes & code Inject CSS, JavaScript, and full code blocks against the 7.1 layout model. 05 Webhooks & automation Subscribe to order, inventory, content, and customer events with signed delivery. 06 AI compatibility Integrate our API docs directly into Claude or ChatGPT. What APIs and tools does the platform include? Get deep control with Commerce APIs, Reseller APIs, and a reliable custom code spec. Commerce APIs Read and write orders, products, inventory, and transactions. REST endpoints, webhooks for order events, and signed payloads for safe server-to-server delivery. â Custom Code Spec A documented contract for injecting code into 7.1 sites â code blocks, code injection points, and the Fluid Engine layout model. No version drift. â Reseller APIs Provision, configure and bill for Squarespace sites and domains on behalf of clients. Built for companies looking to integrate our products into their offering. â Stay in the loop Get notified about API updates, breaking changes, and new developer tools. Email address Sign Up By pressing Sign Up, I consent to receive updates about Squarespace developer tools and acknowledge that my information is subject to the Squarespace Privacy Policy . pages.text: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs Commerce APIs MCP Reseller APIs Templates Custom Code Upcoming Changes Overview Connect a Client Tools Domains Commerce Menu Copy page MCP Overview of the Squarespace MCP Server The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants to Squarespace. It's built on the Model Context Protocol , an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools, so assistants like Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT can look things up and make changes on Squarespace in the middle of a conversation. With it, someone can describe a new business and leave the chat with a domain ready to buy, or ask "which orders still need shipping?" about their own store and get a live answer. Connect a Client â Add Squarespace to Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP client. Notice: If you are a Squarespace user who is accessing the Squarespace MCP server through an AI assistant, for example to search for a domain or manage your own website, your use is governed by our Terms of Service . If you're a developer building an experience for your users and connecting your own app or agent directly to the Squarespace MCP server, for example to add domain search to your product, your use is governed by our Developer Terms of Use . What you can do The server's tools are organized into groups. Each group has its own page describing what its tools do, what to ask for, and what to watch out for. Group What it's for Sign-in Domains Brainstorm business names, check domain availability and pricing, and get a link to buy a domain on Squarespace. Not required Commerce Find, create, and update contacts and products, and look up orders, on one of your websites. Currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. Required How it works The Squarespace MCP server is a remote server. There's nothing to install. Your MCP client connects directly to: Code https://mcp.squarespace.com/mcp You don't call the tools yourself. You ask the assistant for something in plain language, and it decides which tools to call and in what order. The tool descriptions the assistant needs are sent by the server when it connects, so they don't need to be copied into your prompts. Signing in The Domains tools work for anyone, with no Squarespace account required. The Commerce tools read and change a website, so they need you to sign in with your Squarespace account. They only appear in your client once you've signed in, and they act with your own permissions: an assistant can only see and change what you could see and change yourself in that website's Commerce panel. See Connect a Client . Working with a website Every signed-in tool works on one website at a time. If it isn't clear which site you mean, the assistant will ask, then keep using that site for the rest of the conversation until you ask to switch. What the tools can and can't change Domains tools never buy anything. They return a checkout link. A domain is only registered when someone opens that link and completes checkout on squarespace.com. Commerce tools don't move money. They can create and update contacts and products, but they can't take payments, issue refunds, or fulfill orders. Orders are read-only. Changes are real. A product or contact the assistant creates or edits is saved to your live website. New products are hidden from shoppers until you (or the assistant, if you ask) publish them. Most MCP clients ask you to approve a tool before it makes a change. Keep that approval step turned on for tools that write to your website. Supported clients Squarespace is built into Gemini as a connected app, and the Domains tools also work in Claude, ChatGPT, and any client that supports remote MCP servers. The Commerce tools are currently only available in Claude and ChatGPT. See Connect a Client for setup steps. Connect a Client On this page What you can do How it works Signing in Working with a website What the tools can and can't change Supported clients

Optionally filter by email address. Retrieve List of Customers âº query Parameters email â string Filter by customer email address. Must be a valid email format. When provided, returns at most one matching customer and cursor pagination is not applied. limit â integer Â Â·Â int32 Â Â·Â min: 1 Â Â·Â max: 100 Maximum number of customers to return per page. Defaults to 20. Clamped to [1, 100]. Default: 20 offset â string Pagination cursor returned in the previous response's nextPageUrl . Omit to retrieve the first page. Do not construct this value manually. Retrieve List of Customers âº Headers Authorization â string Â Â·Â required API key or OAuth access token Default: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN User-Agent â string Â Â·Â required User Agent Default: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION Retrieve List of Customers âº Responses 200 400 401 500 503 Customers retrieved successfully. Paginated list of customers for the current seller. Customers customers â Customer [] List of customers for the current page. nextPageUrl â string URL to retrieve the next page of results. null when there are no further pages. GET / reseller / v1 / customers curl https://api.squarespace.com/reseller/v1/customers \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN' \ --header 'User-Agent: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION' cURL JavaScript Python Java Go C# Kotlin Objective-C PHP Ruby Swift Example Responses 200 400 401 500 503 { "customers" : [ { "customerId" : "d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc" , "status" : "ACTIVE" , "verificationUrl" : "https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/confirm-account?token=abc123" , "createdOn" : "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z" }, { "customerId" : "e4f5a6b7-8901-bcde-f012-345678901234" , "status" : "PENDING" , "verificationUrl" : "https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/confirm-account?token=def456" , "createdOn" : "2024-01-14T09:00:00Z" } ], "nextPageUrl" : "/reseller/v1/customers?limit=2&offset=eyJ1dWlkIjoiZTRmNWE2YjctODkwMS1iY2RlLWYwMTItMzQ1Njc4OTAxMjM0IiwiaW5zdGFudCI6IjIwMjQtMDEtMTRUMDk6MDA6MDAuMDAwMDAwWiJ9&uu=true" } json Customers found with next page application/json Customers found with next page Last page No customers found Create Customer POST https://api.squarespace.com /reseller/v1/customers Create a new customer under the current seller. A Squarespace account is created and linked asynchronously â the response is returned immediately with status PENDING. Create Customer âº Headers Authorization â string Â Â·Â required API key or OAuth access token Default: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN User-Agent â string Â Â·Â required User Agent Default: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION Create Customer âº Request Body Request body for creating a new customer. CreateCustomerRequest email â string Â Â·Â required Customer email address. Must not already be registered with Squarespace. Max 254 characters. Example: [email protected] firstName â string Â Â·Â minLength: 0 Â Â·Â maxLength: 250 Â Â·Â required Customer first name. Max 250 characters. Example: Jane lastName â string Â Â·Â minLength: 0 Â Â·Â maxLength: 250 Â Â·Â required Customer last name. Max 250 characters. Example: Doe socialAccount â string Â Â·Â enum Â Â·Â required Defines how Squarespace will prompt the user to log in. PASSWORD indicates the customer will be asked to create and use email + password; the others are SSO options. Note customers may change their login method on the Squarespace site. Enum values: APPLE GOOGLE FACEBOOK PASSWORD Example: PASSWORD acceptedAt â string Â Â·Â date-time Timestamp when the customer accepted the terms of service. Required if acceptedTerms is provided. Example: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z acceptedTerms â boolean Whether the customer accepted the terms of service. Required if acceptedAt is provided. locale â string Â Â·Â minLength: 0 Â Â·Â maxLength: 35 Preferred locale for the customer's Squarespace account. Defaults to 'en-US' if omitted. Supports formats such as 'en', 'en-US', 'es-419', 'pt-BR'. Max 35 characters. Example: en-US location â string Â Â·Â minLength: 0 Â Â·Â maxLength: 2 Â Â·Â pattern: ^[A-Z]{2}$ ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the customer's account. Used for regional settings and GDPR. Defaults to the country implied by locale if omitted. Example: US metadata â object Additional key-value metadata for the customer. Keys max 50 characters, values max 255 characters. timezone â string Timezone for the customer's account, as a tz database identifier. Use underscores for multi-word cities (e.g. 'America/New_York'). Example: America/New_York Create Customer âº Responses 200 400 401 403 409 500 Customer created successfully. Account provisioning is in progress. A customer account registered under the current seller. Customer createdOn â string Account creation timestamp. Example: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z customerId â string UUID of the customer account, within the reseller's account Example: d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc email â string Customer email address. Omitted from list responses. status â string Â Â·Â enum Status of the customer's Squarespace account. ACTIVE: valid and operational. PENDING: account creation in progress. SUSPENDED: pending deletion by Squarespace. TERMINATED: account deleted. FAILED: account creation failed. Enum values: ACTIVE PENDING SUSPENDED TERMINATED FAILED Example: ACTIVE verificationUrl â string URL the customer must visit to verify their Squarespace account. This link never expires. POST / reseller / v1 / customers curl https://api.squarespace.com/reseller/v1/customers \ --request POST \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN' \ --header 'User-Agent: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION' \ --data '{ "acceptedAt": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z", "acceptedTerms": true, "email": " [email protected] ", "firstName": "Jane", "lastName": "Doe", "locale": "en-US", "location": "US", "metadata": {}, "socialAccount": "PASSWORD", "timezone": "America/New_York" }' cURL JavaScript Python Java Go C# Kotlin Objective-C PHP Ruby Swift Example Request Body { "acceptedAt" : "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z" , "acceptedTerms" : true , "email" : " [email protected] " , "firstName" : "Jane" , "lastName" : "Doe" , "locale" : "en-US" , "location" : "US" , "metadata" : {}, "socialAccount" : "PASSWORD" , "timezone" : "America/New_York" } json Example Responses 200 400 401 403 409 500 { "customerId" : "d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc" , "email" : " [email protected] " , "status" : "PENDING" , "createdOn" : "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000000Z" } json Customer created application/json Link Customer Account POST https://api.squarespace.com /reseller/v1/customers/link-account Link an existing Squarespace account to the current seller. Use this instead of Create Customer when the customer already has a Squarespace account. This endpoint needs to be called using a token retrieved via the account-linking process â see account-linking guide Link Customer Account âº Headers Authorization â string Â Â·Â required API key or OAuth access token Default: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN User-Agent â string Â Â·Â required User Agent Default: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION Link Customer Account âº Request Body Request body for linking an existing Squarespace account to the current seller. LinkCustomerRequest email â string Â Â·Â required Email address of the existing Squarespace account to link. Must match the account identified by the X-Member-Account-Id header. Example: [email protected] Link Customer Account âº Responses 200 400 401 409 500 Account linked successfully. The status reflects the current state of the Squarespace account. A customer account linked to the current seller. LinkAccountCustomer createdOn â string Timestamp when the customer record was created. Example: 2024-01-15T10:30:00.000000Z customerId â string UUID of the customer account. Example: d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc email â string Customer email address. Example: [email protected] status â string Â Â·Â enum Current status of the customer's Squarespace account. ACTIVE: valid and operational. PENDING: account creation in progress. SUSPENDED: pending deletion. TERMINATED: account deleted. FAILED: account creation failed. Enum values: ACTIVE PENDING SUSPENDED TERMINATED FAILED Example: ACTIVE POST / reseller / v1 / customers / link-account curl https://api.squarespace.com/reseller/v1/customers/link-account \ --request POST \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN' \ --header 'User-Agent: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION' \ --data '{ "email": " [email protected] " }' cURL JavaScript Python Java Go C# Kotlin Objective-C PHP Ruby Swift Example Request Body { "email" : " [email protected] " } json Example Responses 200 400 401 409 500 { "customerId" : "d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc" , "email" : " [email protected] " , "status" : "ACTIVE" , "createdOn" : "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000000Z" } json Account linked application/json Update Customer Email POST https://api.squarespace.com /reseller/v1/customers/update-email Change the email address one of your customers logs in with. The change is accepted and applied asynchronously, so a 202 means it was queued, not that the account is already updated; there is no callback and no status to poll. Watch for the customer and domain events to know it was applied. Sending the address the customer already has is answered 200 instead: there is nothing to queue, so no event is ever emitted and waiting for one would hang. The customer is not notified and the new address is not verified, so confirm it with them before calling. Update Customer Email âº Headers Authorization â string Â Â·Â required API key or OAuth access token Default: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN User-Agent â string Â Â·Â required User Agent Default: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION Update Customer Email âº Request Body Request body for updating the email address of a customer of the current seller. UpdateCustomerEmailRequest customerId â string Â Â·Â uuid Â Â·Â pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9â¦ Â Â·Â required Reseller customer ID whose email should be updated. Example: d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc email â string Â Â·Â required New email address. Must not belong to another Squarespace account; if it does, move the customer's products instead. Example: [email protected] Update Customer Email âº Responses 200 202 400 404 409 500 The customer already logs in with that address. Nothing was queued and no event will be emitted. No data returned POST / reseller / v1 / customers / update-email curl https://api.squarespace.com/reseller/v1/customers/update-email \ --request POST \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN' \ --header 'User-Agent: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION' \ --data '{ "customerId": "d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc", "email": " [email protected] " }' cURL JavaScript Python Java Go C# Kotlin Objective-C PHP Ruby Swift Example Request Body { "customerId" : "d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc" , "email" : " [email protected] " } json Example Responses 200 202 400 404 409 500 No example specified for this content type Retrieve Customer by ID GET https://api.squarespace.com /reseller/v1/customers/{customerId} Retrieve a customer previously created by the current seller. Returns richer profile data than the list endpoint, including name, email, language, timezone, and account verification status. Retrieve Customer by ID âº path Parameters customerId â string Â Â·Â uuid Â Â·Â required Reseller customer ID. Retrieve Customer by ID âº Headers Authorization â string Â Â·Â required API key or OAuth access token Default: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN User-Agent â string Â Â·Â required User Agent Default: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION Retrieve Customer by ID âº Responses 200 400 401 404 500 Customer retrieved successfully. Profile information for a reseller customer. CustomerProfile country â string Country code derived from the customer's preferred locale. Defaults to 'US'. Example: US createdOn â string Timestamp when the customer account was created. Example: 2024-01-15T10:30:00Z customerId â string UUID of the customer account. Example: d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc email â string Customer email address. Omitted from the response if not available. firstName â string Customer first name. Example: John language â string Language code derived from the customer's preferred locale. Defaults to 'en'. Example: en lastName â string Customer last name. Example: Smith region â string Always empty. status â string Â Â·Â enum Customer account status. Enum values: PENDING ACTIVE TERMINATED Example: ACTIVE timezone â string Customer timezone. Defaults to 'America/New_York'. Example: America/New_York verificationUrl â string URL the customer must visit to verify their account. GET / reseller / v1 / customers / {customerId} curl https://api.squarespace.com/reseller/v1/customers/:customerId \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY_OR_OAUTH_TOKEN' \ --header 'User-Agent: YOUR_CUSTOM_APP_DESCRIPTION' cURL JavaScript Python Java Go C# Kotlin Objective-C PHP Ruby Swift Example Responses 200 400 401 404 500 { "customerId" : "d3c4e5f6-7890-abcd-ef01-234567890abc" , "email" : " [email protected] " , "firstName" : "John" , "lastName" : "Smith" , "language" : "en" , "country" : "US" , "region" : "" , "timezone" : "America/New_York" , "status" : "ACTIVE" , "verificationUrl" : "https://login.squarespace.com/api/1/login/confirm-account?token=abc123" , "createdOn" : "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z" , "accountVerified" : true } json Active customer application/json ccTLD Edge Cases Pricing

pages.text: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs Commerce APIs MCP Reseller APIs Templates Custom Code Upcoming Changes Start Here Quick Start Beginner Tutorial The Basics Template Files Template Language Squarespace Tags JavaScript Advanced Menu Copy page Start Here Quick Start The Squarespace Developer Platform enables web developers to access Squarespace template files (as provided to the consumer) and customize those files to create something unique. The advanced developer can go even further and create his or her own custom template from scratch. Notice: Use of the Squarespace Developer Platform is subject to our Developer Terms of Use . Choose a Starting Point First, you can start with one of the consumer level templates created by Squarespace's designers. These templates have loads of style options built-in, allowing you to achieve a high quality design quickly. If you've already started a Squarespace site and you want to enable Developer Mode, jump to step two. Start With a Consumer Template Or optionally, you can start with the developer Base Template, which features very minimal styles and markup used to create a completely custom template. Start With Developer Base Template NOTE: Trial sites with Developer Mode enabled do not expire, giving you as much time as you need to build your custom Squarespace site. Enable Developer Mode Enabling Developer Mode will give you access to a copy of the template repository for your site, allowing you to make changes to the template and add custom code using Git. Note: Your site will not receive template updates from Squarespace when Developer Mode is enabled, and you will not be able to switch templates. Additionally, note that using Git will not allow you to run server-side code. Before enabling Developer Mode, itâs important to note that disabling Developer Mode (or disconnecting GitHub Repository) is an irreversible action. You can expect the following if you disable it in the future: Any changes to the template repository including custom collections, new or modified layouts and regions, new or modified scripts and styles, uploaded assets and custom types will be lost. All tweaks in the Site Styles panel will revert to their original settings before Developer Mode was enabled. All content in block fields such as sidebars, headers and footers will be lost. Existing content items based on custom types will still be editable as their base content items but without the custom fields. The site's existing navigation structure will revert to the original navigation structure. Pages from the existing navigation structure will be moved to the Not Linked section of the Pages panel. Existing custom collections will become uneditable. If youâve decided to move forward with turning on Developer Mode, in the Site Manager, navigate to Settings -> Developer Tools -> Developer Mode . At the top right corner of the settings panel, there is a toggle that is set to off. Click the toggle to turn on Developer Mode. For new Developer Mode sites, the steps to connect to Git are: Click Connect to GitHub Authorize connection Name repository To migrate an existing site to GitHub you will click a link in the banner of the Developer Mode panel and follow the same steps Contact Customer Care for help and troubleshooting Git connection. pages.text: Squarespace Developer Platform: APIs, Apps, and Docs Commerce APIs MCP Reseller APIs Templates Custom Code Upcoming Changes Custom Code Specification About HTML Attributes CSS Variables Menu Copy page Custom Code Specification Custom Code Specification The Custom Code Specification is a set of persistent HTML and CSS properties that you can rely on when adding custom code to a Squarespace website. Squarespace is constantly evolving and releasing new features for our websites. This can cause the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript powering Squarespace websites to change unexpectedly, which may affect how your custom code works. To maximize the stability of your custom code, use only the properties outlined in this Specification. HTML attributes, DOM structure, CSS selectors, CSS variables, and JavaScript variables that are not in the Custom Code Specification are more likely to change in ways that could break custom code.
